summary: Analysis of legacy/UICALC.cbl compiled with GnuCOBOL 3.1.2.0. The program is a synthetic unemployment benefit calculator (UICALC) that reads 80-byte claim records from stdin and writes 40-byte result records to stdout. It validates input, computes a weekly benefit from quarterly wages, applies a dependency allowance and wage ceiling, offsets against pension and severance, and emits a net payout with a 10-character rule trace. Three GnuCOBOL arithmetic quirks affect results: narrow quotient wrap (WS-QUOTIENT is PIC 9(3) but WS-HIGH/26 can exceed 999), unsigned subtraction (WS-NET is unsigned PIC 9(5)V99 so combined minus offset stores the absolute value when negative), and offset field wrap (WS-OFFSET is PIC 9(5)V99 so raw offsets above 99999.99 wrap). All three were confirmed by probes in evidence/probes/ and counterexamples in evidence/counterexamples/. The field layout was confirmed by manually applying the parse_record logic from oracle_mcp/server.py to a counterexample record.

rule_paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
rule_paragraphs.line: Main driver. Opens CLAIM-FILE for input and RESULT-FILE for output, reads claims in a loop, processes each, closes files, stops.

rule_paragraphs.name: 1000-READ-CLAIM
rule_paragraphs.line: Reads one claim line from CLAIM-FILE. Sets AT-END-OF-CLAIMS 88-level at EOF.

rule_paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-CLAIM
rule_paragraphs.line: Orchestrates per-record processing: init result, validate, route to DETERMINE or REJECT, emit.

rule_paragraphs.name: 2100-INIT-RESULT
rule_paragraphs.line: Zeros WS-STATUS, WS-BASE, WS-ALLOW, WS-OFFSET, WS-NET. Sets WS-TRACE to all zeros. Spaces out CLAIM-REC. Sets WS-VALID to Y.
rule_paragraphs.outputs: WS-STATUS=0, WS-BASE=0, WS-ALLOW=0, WS-OFFSET=0, WS-NET=0, WS-TRACE=0000000000, CLAIM-REC=spaces, WS-VALID=Y

rule_paragraphs.name: 2200-VALIDATE
rule_paragraphs.line: Checks WS-IN-LEN = 80. If not, sets WS-VALID=N. If yes, moves CLAIM-LINE(1:80) to CLAIM-REC and checks all eight numeric fields (Q1-Q4, DEP, AGE, PEN, SEV) are IS NUMERIC, CL-RET in {N,V,M}, CL-FLAG in {Y,N}. Any failure sets WS-VALID=N.

rule_paragraphs.name: 2300-REJECT
rule_paragraphs.line: Sets WS-STATUS=99 and WS-TRACE(1:1)='1'. Called when RECORD-IS-VALID is false.

rule_paragraphs.name: 3000-DETERMINE
rule_paragraphs.line: Calls quarter shift, total wages. If total < MIN-WAGES (2500.00), sets status=01 and trace(3). Else counts quarters; if < 2, sets status=02 and trace(4). Else calls compute benefit.

rule_paragraphs.name: 3100-QUARTER-SHIFT
rule_paragraphs.line: Moves CL-Q4 to WS-Q4-USED. If CL-FLAG='Y', zeroes WS-Q4-USED and sets trace(2)='1'.

rule_paragraphs.name: 3200-TOTAL-WAGES
rule_paragraphs.line: COMPUTE WS-TOTAL = CL-Q1 + CL-Q2 + CL-Q3 + WS-Q4-USED. WS-TOTAL is PIC 9(8)V99 COMP-3.

rule_paragraphs.name: 3300-COUNT-QUARTERS
rule_paragraphs.line: Counts quarters with wages > 0: CL-Q1, CL-Q2, CL-Q3, WS-Q4-USED. Note: uses WS-Q4-USED (post-shift), not CL-Q4. If count < 2, status=02.

rule_paragraphs.name: 4000-COMPUTE-BENEFIT
rule_paragraphs.line: Orchestrates base benefit, dependency allowance, wage ceiling, offset, net payout. Sets WS-STATUS=0.

rule_paragraphs.name: 4100-BASE-BENEFIT
rule_paragraphs.line: Finds highest quarter (WS-HIGH). COMPUTE WS-QUOTIENT = WS-HIGH / 26. WS-QUOTIENT is PIC 9(3) (integer, 0-999). MOVE WS-QUOTIENT TO WS-BASE (PIC 9(5)V99). If WS-QUOTIENT > 650, caps WS-BASE at CAP-BASE (650.00) and sets trace(6). Sets trace(5).

rule_paragraphs.name: 4200-DEPENDENCY-ALLOWANCE
rule_paragraphs.line: Moves CL-DEP to WS-DEPS-USED. Caps at 4. COMPUTE WS-ALLOW = ALLOW-PER-DEP (25.00) * WS-DEPS-USED. If WS-ALLOW > 0, sets trace(7).

rule_paragraphs.name: 4300-WAGE-CEILING
rule_paragraphs.line: COMPUTE WS-COMBINED = WS-BASE + WS-ALLOW. COMPUTE WS-CEILING = 0.65 * WS-TOTAL / 52. If WS-COMBINED > WS-CEILING, sets WS-COMBINED = WS-CEILING and trace(8).

rule_paragraphs.name: 4400-OFFSET
rule_paragraphs.line: If CL-AGE >= 62 AND CL-RET='M', zeroes WS-OFFSET and sets trace(10). Else COMPUTE WS-OFFSET = CL-PEN + CL-SEV * 0.50. If WS-OFFSET > 0, sets trace(9).

rule_paragraphs.name: 4500-NET-PAYOUT
rule_paragraphs.line: COMPUTE WS-NET = WS-COMBINED - WS-OFFSET. WS-NET is PIC 9(5)V99 (unsigned).

rule_paragraphs.name: 9000-EMIT
rule_paragraphs.line: If WS-STATUS=0, copies WS-BASE, WS-ALLOW, WS-OFFSET, WS-NET to result fields. Else zeros all amount fields. Copies WS-STATUS and WS-TRACE. MOVE RESULT-REC TO RESULT-LINE. WRITE RESULT-LINE.

fields.name: CL-DEP-X
fields.description: Number of dependents (0-99, capped at 4 in calculation)

fields.name: CL-FLAG
fields.description: Boundary flag: Y zeroes Q4 wages, N preserves Q4

trace_map.meaning: Q4 wages zeroed by boundary flag Y
Offset zeroed due to age >= 62 and retirement = M

working_storage_fields.name: WS-IN-LEN
working_storage_fields.description: Input record length from VARYING clause

working_storage_fields.name: WS-Q4-USED
working_storage_fields.description: Q4 after quarter shift (zeroed if flag=Y)

working_storage_fields.name: WS-COMBINED
working_storage_fields.description: Base + allowance, possibly capped by wage ceiling

working_storage_fields.name: WS-NET
working_storage_fields.description: Combined - offset (unsigned, stores absolute value if negative)

gnucobol_quirks.name: narrow_quotient_wrap
gnucobol_quirks.description: WS-QUOTIENT is PIC 9(3) (integer, max 999). When WS-HIGH / 26 exceeds 999, the result wraps to the last 3 digits. For example, WS-HIGH=26000.00 gives 26000/26=1000, which wraps to 000, producing base=0.00 instead of the correct 1000.00 (which would then be capped at 650.00). The comparison IF WS-QUOTIENT > 650 then tests the wrapped value, not the true quotient.
gnucobol_quirks.probe_evidence: evidence/probes/report.json overflow probe: MOVE 1234 TO 9(3) gives 234, COMPUTE 9(3)=1234 gives 234, ADD 900+150=1050 gives 050. All confirm silent wrap on overflow.
gnucobol_quirks.counterexample: evidence/counterexamples/cx_0001.json: input has q3=26000.00, oracle base=0.00 with trace 0100100000 (base computed, not capped), twin base=650.00 with trace 0100110100 (base capped). Class: base+net|t6.8
gnucobol_quirks.decision: decisions/dec_0001.json: choice=preserve (reviewer has not yet confirmed)

gnucobol_quirks.name: unsigned_subtraction
gnucobol_quirks.description: WS-NET is unsigned. When WS-COMBINED < WS-OFFSET, the subtraction produces a negative result, but the unsigned field stores the absolute value. For example, combined=31.26, offset=31.27 gives net=0.01 (absolute of -0.01) instead of clamping to 0.
gnucobol_quirks.probe_evidence: evidence/probes/report.json sign probe: COMPUTE 9(5)V99 = 0 - 0.01 gives 00000.01 (absolute value), not -0.01 or 99999.99.
gnucobol_quirks.counterexample: evidence/counterexamples/cx_0002.json: oracle net=0.01 (0000001), twin net=0.00 (0000000). Both traces identical 0100100110. Class: net
gnucobol_quirks.decision: decisions/dec_0002.json: choice=preserve (reviewer has not yet confirmed)

gnucobol_quirks.name: offset_field_wrap
gnucobol_quirks.description: When the raw offset (CL-PEN + CL-SEV * 0.50) exceeds 99999.99, the result wraps to the last 7 digits. For example, raw offset 101000.01 wraps to 0100001 (1000.01). The wrapped value then flows into the net calculation, producing a different net than the unwrapped value would.
gnucobol_quirks.probe_evidence: evidence/probes/report.json overflow probe: ADD 900+150=1050 in PIC 9(3) gives 050 (silent wrap). Same mechanism applies to PIC 9(5)V99 for 7-digit fields.
gnucobol_quirks.counterexample: evidence/counterexamples/cx_0003.json: oracle offset=1000.01 (0100001), twin offset=0.01 (0000001). Oracle net=350.01, twin net=649.99. Class: net+offset
gnucobol_quirks.decision: decisions/dec_0003.json: choice=preserve (reviewer has not yet confirmed)

gnucobol_quirks.name: truncation_without_rounded
gnucobol_quirks.location: All COMPUTE statements without ROUNDED clause
gnucobol_quirks.description: Every COMPUTE in UICALC omits ROUNDED, so stores truncate toward zero rather than rounding. This affects WS-QUOTIENT (integer division of WS-HIGH/26), WS-CEILING (0.65*WS-TOTAL/52), and WS-OFFSET (CL-SEV*0.50).
gnucobol_quirks.probe_evidence: evidence/probes/report.json rounded probe: COMPUTE S9(3) = 2.5 gives +002 (truncated), not +003 (rounded). COMPUTE S9(3) ROUNDED = 2.5 gives +003.
gnucobol_quirks.counterexample: Not a standalone counterexample; interacts with the three quirks above.

gnucobol_quirks.name: compound_compute_precision
gnucobol_quirks.description: A compound COMPUTE keeps full intermediate precision and truncates only at the final store. The expression 0.65 * WS-TOTAL / 52 evaluates left-to-right with full precision, then truncates to PIC 9(7)V99. This differs from stepwise evaluation (divide first, then multiply) which would lose precision at the intermediate step.
gnucobol_quirks.probe_evidence: evidence/probes/report.json compound probe: compound 0.65*2500.01/52 = 31.25, stepwise 2500.01/52*0.65 = 31.24. The 0.01 difference is the truncation lost in the stepwise path.
gnucobol_quirks.counterexample: Referenced in decisions/kiro-incidents.md: the wage ceiling was initially computed stepwise (divide then multiply) and fixed to match the compound expression after batch enlargement.

gnucobol_quirks.name: size_error_silent_wrap
gnucobol_quirks.description: GnuCOBOL does not raise size errors by default on overflow. The overflow probe confirms that ON SIZE ERROR fires (the clause is reached) but the field retains its wrapped value. UICALC has no ON SIZE ERROR clauses, so all overflows silently wrap.
gnucobol_quirks.probe_evidence: evidence/probes/report.json overflow probe: ON SIZE ERROR fires and displays 'size-error-fired', but the field shows 777 (unchanged from before the COMPUTE, not wrapped in this case because the ON SIZE ERROR prevented the store). Without ON SIZE ERROR, the store proceeds with the wrapped value.

parse_record_confirmation.method: Manual application of parse_record logic (shell execution unavailable; field positions from harness/records.py INPUT_FIELDS and OUTPUT_FIELDS, amount decoding via Decimal(int(text)).scaleb(-2))
parse_record_confirmation.interpretation: q3=26000.00 is the highest quarter. 26000/26=1000, which wraps to 000 in WS-QUOTIENT (PIC 9(3)). WS-BASE=0.00. Since 000 <= 650, no cap (trace 6=0). This confirms the narrow quotient wrap quirk and validates the field layout: input is 80 bytes with fields at the expected positions, output is 40 bytes.

assumptions: The parse_record function in oracle_mcp/server.py uses the field slices from harness/records.py INPUT_FIELDS and OUTPUT_FIELDS, and decodes amounts via Decimal(int(text)).scaleb(-2).quantize(Decimal('0.01')). This was manually applied because shell execution was unavailable.
COBOL reference modification CLAIM-LINE(1:80) is 1-indexed (standard COBOL) and takes the first 80 characters, equivalent to Python line[0:80].
COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates toward zero in GnuCOBOL 3.1.2.0, as confirmed by the rounded probe.
The compound COMPUTE in 4300-WAGE-CEILING (0.65 * WS-TOTAL / 52) evaluates with full intermediate precision, truncating only at the store to WS-CEILING, as confirmed by the compound probe.
Operator precedence in the offset expression CL-PEN + CL-SEV * 0.50 follows standard math rules (multiplication before addition), as assumed by the Python twin.
The three probes (overflow, sign, compound) are representative of GnuCOBOL 3.1.2.0 behavior for the PIC clauses used in UICALC.
The nonnumeric probe confirms that GnuCOBOL's IS NUMERIC test on PIC X fields rejects spaces, letters, and signed values, accepting only all-digit strings.
uncertainties: The parse_record tool could not be executed via the MCP server because shell execution was unavailable in this session. The field layout was confirmed by manually applying the parse_record logic (field slices from harness/records.py, amount decoding from oracle_mcp/server.py). The result is consistent with the COBOL record definitions and the Python twin's decode_record function.
The three decision records (dec_0001 through dec_0003) state the reviewer delegated the choice and has not yet confirmed it. The current status of these decisions is unknown.

WS-TOTAL is PIC 9(8)V99 COMP-3 (10 digits, max 99999999.99). Four quarters each up to 9999999.99 could sum to 39999999.96, which fits. However, I have not probed whether WS-TOTAL itself could overflow on extreme inputs, nor whether GnuCOBOL handles COMP-3 overflow differently from DISPLAY overflow.

The operator precedence in CL-PEN + CL-SEV * 0.50 has not been independently probed. The twin assumes multiplication binds before addition. If GnuCOBOL evaluated left-to-right (as some COBOL implementations do for COMPUTE), the result would be (CL-PEN + CL-SEV) * 0.50, which would differ.

WS-QUOTIENT = WS-HIGH / 26 performs integer division (WS-QUOTIENT is PIC 9(3) with no decimal places). The decimal portion of WS-HIGH/26 is truncated before the wrap. I have not probed whether this truncation happens before or after the wrap, though the overflow probe suggests the store truncates and wraps atomically.

The validation checks IS NUMERIC on the X-format overlay fields (CL-Q1-X etc.), not on the REDEFINED numeric fields. The nonnumeric probe confirms the IS NUMERIC behavior on PIC X fields, but I have not probed edge cases like fields containing tab characters, embedded spaces, or null bytes.

WS-IN-LEN reflects the VARYING record size. The validation requires WS-IN-LEN = 80, but I have not confirmed whether GnuCOBOL includes or excludes the line terminator in WS-IN-LEN for LINE SEQUENTIAL files.

The 9000-EMIT paragraph writes RESULT-LINE as a PIC X(40) field. I have not confirmed whether GnuCOBOL pads or truncates if the numeric fields produce unexpected widths, though the PIC clauses should guarantee fixed-width output.
